title: Grappelli's film records, Sugar Ray Robinson's entourage, and francs to Belgium
summary: He recorded for a Grappelli film that was shot after he left; in Paris he took June Clark to dinner and found a way to send francs to Belgium and then home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Stephane Grappelli was nice. I had another week off which, after the two weeks I did there. That was really finishing all that he had promised me, the four weeks. I had another week off. Stephane Grappelli got a picture together. He got a picture and he got me in there to make the records. We made the records for the picture and everything. And you know, they take their time over there. At least at that time they did. And instead of them shooting the picture, they're going to shoot the picture later. They'll let you know when they get ready to shoot the picture. So when they got ready to shoot the picture, I was on my way in Belgium, you know. And so it just happened that Ray Robinson come in town. And oh, he's got this big entourage with him, and June Clark happened to be with him. And it looked like they was giving him short money or something, so I would take him to dinner while I was there, you know.

June, yeah. Well, June had been around a long time, and he had it rough. He was just like one of the hangers on, you know. He was used to having all this money they'd give him to eat off of and stuff. I said, 'Don't worry about that.' I was taking him francs and stowing them away in the safe deposit box in the hotel, because I found out what to do. Now, you take all this stuff, all these francs. The francs was a whole lot. You got a whole lot of francs for a dollar, you know, and take it to Belgium and send it right on
over here. See, you couldn't take it out of France.
But I could take it to Belgium and they change it up for you and send it right here, and the next morning she would have it.
